gnss_l1_gps_glonass.notes: Uncalibrated SDRs should treat raised noise, swept tones, or coherent GNSS-like replicas differently. GLONASS L1 spans around 1598-1609 MHz, while GPS L1 is centered at 1575.42 MHz.

gsm_cellular_800_960.notes: Cellular, ISM/RC, and drone-jammer signatures overlap in this region. Raster, duplex pairing, and burst framing are critical discriminators.

gsm_cellular_1800_1900.notes: Likely cellular if OFDM/GSM raster and duplex pairing are visible; likely jammer if broad noise or swept carriers blanket multiple paired allocations.

ism_433.notes: Very high false-positive band. Short OOK/FSK bursts are usually civilian ISM; sustained barrage noise suggests jammer.

ism_868_915.notes: Hop/chirp structure helps separate ELRS/Crossfire/LoRa from broadband jammers and civilian LoRaWAN.

wifi_bt_rc_fpv_2g4.notes: This is a dense shared band. OFDM channel width points to Wi-Fi/DJI; LoRa/FLRC/FHSS points to RC control; broadband noise points to jammer.

wifi_fpv_5g8.notes: Analog FPV is usually fixed-channel wide FM-like video around 5.6-5.9 GHz; digital FPV/Wi-Fi use OFDM-like channels. 5.8 GHz is also a common jammer band.

starlink_leo_satcom_ku.notes: Terminal uplink is directional and in Ku-band; downlink may be satellite-origin rather than terminal-origin. Starlink attribution requires timing/channel behavior, direction/elevation, and local terminal Wi-Fi correlation.

satcom_lband_inmarsat_iridium.notes: Inmarsat downlink is near 1525-1559 MHz, uplink near 1626.5-1660.5 MHz; Iridium occupies about 1616-1626.5 MHz. Adjacent GNSS/GLONASS observations can confound.
